decreases monotonically with increasing temperature; collapses steeply between ~600 and 800 °C; by 800 °C converges to 0–100 MPa

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon atmosphere within a radiation furnace; 30 min hold at testing temperature; NiCr-Ni thermocouple on specimen surface
characterization_methods.purpose: determine yield stress and stress-strain behaviour at room and elevated temperatures
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C room-temperature compression yield stress 827 MPa; tension-compression asymmetry observed

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530 with 20 kV, working distance 15 mm, secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fracture surfaces of ruptured tensile specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (Fig. 4d): coarse transgranular cleavage facets with elongated plates; mode TGC (transgranular cleavage)

unmapped_findings: Room-temperature fracture mode of Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C is transgranular cleavage (TGC) (Table 2, Fig. 4d).
Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C has higher matrix hardness but lower yield stress in compression than Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C (b0023).

In room-temperature tension, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (Fig. 3, curve 4) showed linear elastic loading followed by abrupt load drop, peaking around the 500 MPa gridline; yield stress in tension and total elongation are reported as '-' in Table 2.

At elevated temperatures, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (Nb-containing) shows the highest strength among Fe-15Al-based alloys at all tested temperatures; its compressive yield stress decreases monotonically with temperature with no yield stress anomaly (Fig. 5, b0038).
At 800 °C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C exhibits tension-compression asymmetry (compression yield stress higher than tension), consistent with all investigated alloys (Fig. 8, b0040).
The Nb- and Ta-containing Fe-15Al-based alloys show the highest strengthening effects in room-temperature compression (b0025).
